4. On the other hand Mr Amit Talukder, the learned Deputy Attorney-General by filing affidavit in opposition on behalf of the Respondent No. 1 submits that the petitioner failed to arrange the monthly meetings of Parishad i.e. January, February and April of 2015. Section 13(2) of the Upazilla Parishad Act, 1998 provides that the Chairman shall be removed if he fails to attend in three monthly meetings consecutively. The present petitioner neither held the monthly meeting nor he was present in the monthly meeting consecutively. Thereafter due to his long absence and retraining from discharging duties, the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer, Savar informed the said matter to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and then the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka investigated the said matter and after getting report, the said report was sent to the Ministry of LGRD and then the Respondent No. 1 initiated the process of removal and accordingly a show cause notice was issued to the petitioner but the petitioner failed to reply with reasonable and cogent ground for his absence. The Government removed the petitioner from the post of the Chairman on 22-6-2015 for public interest under section 13(2) of the Upazilla Parishad Act, 1998. Against the said order of removal, the petitioner did not file Review application within 30 days from the date of removal and thus, the said post of the Chairman became vacant and then, Election Commission declared election schedule for the post of the Chairman of Savar Upazilla Parishad as per law on 6-6-2017. After declaration of election schedule, the petitioner filed Review application to the Respondent No. 1 which is barred by limitation since he is failed to file review application within 30 days as per section 13(4) of the Upazilla Parishad Ain, 1998. At the time of hearing the petitioner failed to submit reasonable ground for his absence and, as such, the review application was rejected on 25-9-2017. He submits that intention of the legislature was that the Chairman of the Upazilla Parishad will discharge their duties continuously and shall arrange the monthly meetings of the Parishad for the said purpose. Therefore the legislature/Parliament enacted the Upazilla Parishad Ain, 1998 providing section 13(1)(Ka) and 13(1)(cha) of the said Upazilla Parishad Act of 1998 in which it is provided that the Chairman shall be removed if the Chairman fails to be present in three monthly meetings consecutively and the Chairman fails to attend minimum 9 monthly meetings out of 12 monthly meetings without giving reasonable ground. It is clear that the Chairman has to attend in three monthly meetings and must arrange the monthly meetings. In this case the petitioner failed to arrange monthly meetings consecutively and also failed to be present in the three meetings and, as such, the Rule is to be discharged. The petitioner failed to arrange three meetings and also failed to be present in the two meetings in such situation the Rule is to be discharged. He further referred section 13(1)(Ka) of the Upazilla Parishad Act, 1998 which provides that a Chairman shall be removed if he is absent three monthly meeting consecutively. In this case the petitioner failed to arrange three monthly meetings i.e. January, February and April of 2015 and also failed to be present in the two meetings i.e. March and May of 2015. Therefore it is clear that the petitioner was absent in the three monthly meeting consecutively. Therefore the petitioner was removed from the post of the Chairman and subsequent application for review was rejected. Under such facts and circumstances the Rule is to be discharged. 

 5. Mr Yousuf Hossain Humayun along with Mr Md Zakir Hossain Sarder the learned advocates by filing affidavit in opposition on behalf of the added Respondent No. 8 submits that the petitioner since was absent in the office from January, 2015 as Chairman and he failed to hold monthly meeting of the Upazilla Parishad from January to April, 2015 and he remained absent and failed to present in the meeting as Chairman, thus the procedure of removal of the petitioner is totally lawful. Further he submits that the petitioner did not discharge his duties properly and tried to make the office ineffective. Therefore the Election Commission declared Election schedule for Savar Upazilla Parishad on 6-6-2017. It is further stated that the petitioner failed to arrange the monthly meetings of Parishad i.e. January, February and April, 2015. Section 13 of the Upazilla Parishad Act, 1998 provides that the Chairman shall be removed if he fails to attend in three monthly meetings consecutively. The present petitioner neither held the monthly meeting nor he was present in the monthly meeting consecutively. Thereafter due to his long absence and retaining from discharging duties, the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer, Savar informed the said matter to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka by his letter dated 13-5-2015 and then the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka investigated the said matter and after getting report, the said report was sent to the Ministry of LGRD on 1-6-2015 and then the Respondent No. 1 initiated the process of removal and accordingly a show cause notice was issued to the petitioner but the petitioner failed to reply with reasonable and cogent ground for his absence rather he admitted the allegation and in the interest of public the petitioner was removed under section 13(2) of the Upazilla Parishad Act, 1998. Against the said order of removal, the petitioner did not file Review application within 30 days from the date of removal and thus the said post of the Chairman became vacant and, as such, the Election Commission declared election schedule for the post of the Chairman of Savar Upazilla Parishad as per law on 6-6-2017. The petitioner filed Review application which is barred by limitation since he is failed to file review application within 30 days as per section 13(4) of the Upazilla Parishad Ain, 1998. At the time of hearing the petitioner failed to submit reasonable grounds for his absence and, as such, the review application was rejected on 25-9-2017. If the chairman fails to remain present in three monthly meetings consecutively and if the Chairman fails to attend minimum 9 monthly meetings out of 12 monthly meetings without giving reasonable ground he can be removed, therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. The respondents has rightly removed the petitioner from the post of the Chairman and rejected the Review application and, as such, the Rule is to be discharged. The petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 7038 of 2015 over the self same matter and that was disposed off and directed the petitioner to go for review. The petitioner also filed another writ petition No. 8792 of 2017 challenging the election schedule which is still pending for hearing. Under such circumstances the Rule is to be discharged.
